---

## Merge verdict: READY

Slice B is coherent and correct. All six mutation sites follow the B4 reference pattern faithfully — I found no cross-site drift, no atomicity hole, no post-commit side-effect on an error path, and no secret leakage. The three accumulated per-task findings are test/doc gaps only (no correctness bug), safely deferrable. No new blocking findings.

### Cross-site consistency (focus #1) — all six verified

| Site | one corr id | write+enqueue+record on same `&*tx` | post-commit awaited & success-only | no-op emits nothing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| role grant/revoke (`roles.rs:221-303`) | ✓ (`corr` binding) | ✓ | ✓ bump; revoke gated on `existed` | ✓ `revoke_in==false` |
| policy put/delete (`policies.rs:122-206`) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ bump gated on `!Absorbed`/`existed` | ✓ Absorbed/`!existed` |
| api-key issue/revoke (`api_keys.rs:247-354`) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ evict post-commit, unconditional-by-design (security) | ✓ revoke gated; evict intentionally unconditional |
| SA create/archive (`service_accounts.rs:155-233`) | ✓ (single event) | ✓ | ✓ archive evict post-commit | duplicate-name rolls back pre-enqueue ✓ |
| create_user (`create_user.rs:114-128`) | ✓ (single event) | ✓ | n/a (outbox-only) | dup-email rolls back pre-enqueue ✓ |

- **Atomicity (focus #2):** every `_in` write (`grant_in`/`put_in`/`delete_in`/`issue_in`/`revoke_in`/`create_in`/`create_user_in`/`set_principal_status_in`) plus `PgOutbox::enqueue`/`PgAuditLog::record` operate on the `recover_txn(tx)`-recovered transaction; the only `&self.db` uses are read methods. Any `?` between the aggregate write and `commit()` propagates, dropping the `Box<dyn Transaction>` → rollback (proven in `outbox_uow_pg.rs` scenario 2). Post-commit bumps/evicts are all after `tx.commit().await?`.
- **Savepoint (focus #3):** `pg_policies.rs:227-267` opens the savepoint via `txn.begin()` off the recovered `&DatabaseTransaction`, `sp.rollback()` on unique-violation, then re-reads on the **same outer txn**. Because the UoW txn is default READ COMMITTED (`db.begin()`), the re-read sees the committed winner → correct absorb-vs-Conflict. Proven under real concurrency in `authz_policy_store.rs` (`put_in_absorbs_a_same_content_savepoint_conflict_and_the_outer_txn_stays_usable`), including that the outer txn still commits afterward.
- **Relay (focus #4):** `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` + partial index `(id) WHERE published_at IS NULL AND parked=false` matches the poll; parked rows excluded; poison-park at `max_attempts`. The batch-wide double-publish window on crash is genuine at-least-once and nothing worse (an `active.update`/`commit` failure rolls back the whole tick → redelivery, no loss/skip). Covered by `relay_pg.rs` scenarios 1-3.
- **Boundary/security (focus #5):** application layer has **no** `Generations` import (only the `PolicyGenBumper` port; comment-only mentions). API-key issue payload/detail carry only `key_id/prefix/scope/status/expires_at` — asserted with an exact key-set test and a plaintext-substring negative (`api_keys.rs:558`).

### Accumulated-findings triage

1. **B6 (Important) — no dedicated PG atomicity test for api-key `issue_in`/`revoke_in` + PgOutbox/PgAuditLog → DEFER (acceptable).** `issue_in`/`revoke_in` are structurally single-statement txn-scoped writes identical to `grant_in` (covered by the B10 e2e), and `PgOutbox`+`PgAuditLog` atomicity is proven generically in `outbox_uow_pg.rs`. Residual risk is low; a dedicated test would be a good follow-up but is not merge-blocking.
2. **B6 (Minor) — `ApiKeyRepository::revoke()` port doc not updated for Ok-on-missing idempotency → DEFER.** Confirmed: `ports.rs:255` has no doc comment while `revoke_in` (256-265) is fully documented. Pure doc nit.
3. **B8 (Minor) — `row_to_domain_event` malformed-row branches untested → DEFER.** Confirmed: `relay.rs:60` has no unit test module. Directly unit-testable with a hand-built `event_outbox::Model`; the parked-row relay tests exercise the failure→park path but not the three malformed-parse branches specifically.

### New observations (non-blocking, notes only)

- **Bootstrap-admin grants emit neither outbox nor audit rows** (`pg_role_grants.rs:142` one-shot `grant()` retained for `BootstrapAdminSeeder`, wired at `http/mod.rs:464`). This is deliberate — event/audit construction lives at the application layer that holds actor/context, and the e2e itself notes the seeder "bypasses `RoleService::grant`." Consistent with the create_user "outbox-only, actor NULL" precedent, but if the compliance intent is *every* committed role grant lands in `audit_log`, a system-actor audit for bootstrap grants is a reasonable future follow-up.
- **Relay holds `FOR UPDATE` locks on the whole batch across sequential `publish().await`s** (`relay.rs:120-145`). Harmless with `TracingEventPublisher` (instant); worth revisiting when a real (slow) broker publisher lands, to avoid long-held locks / transaction bloat. Out of scope for this slice (broker deferred).

All three deferred items are test/doc-only; none affects correctness of the write path, savepoint, relay, or security boundary. Recommend merging and tracking the B6-Important test as a fast follow.

input.content:
**Part of SMA-446** (M5 · IAM v1). This is **Slice B** of sub-project 1 (IAM audit log + outbox), building on the merged **Slice A** (#80, persistent denial audit + query API). It does **not** close the epic — the AI Gateway integration and the dashboards/RUNBOOK sub-projects still follow.

## What this delivers

An application-owned **Unit-of-Work** write path so every committed IAM mutation is atomic and observable.

- **Atomic mutation + event + audit:** each mutation (role grant/revoke, policy put/delete, api-key issue/revoke, principal create/archive) writes its aggregate row, a **domain-event outbox** row, and — for role/key/policy — a **committed `audit_log`** row, in **one Postgres transaction**, all sharing one **correlation id** (so the trail is stitchable end-to-end).
- **Transactional outbox + relay:** a background relay drains `event_outbox` with `SELECT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` (multi-replica-safe, no double-processing), publishes via an `EventPublisher` port (`TracingEventPublisher` for now), marks `published_at`, and parks poison rows after `max_attempts`. At-least-once delivery.
- **Post-commit, awaited side-effects:** the Redis `policy_gen` bump and the api-key validation-cache eviction run **after** commit, awaited, and **never** for a rolled-back mutation — preserving M3's AC1 (a grant is visible to the very next decision) and the security-critical cache eviction on revoke/archive.
- **Savepoints:** `PolicyStore::put`'s conflict-absorption (same-content → absorb, different-content → `Conflict`) is preserved *inside* the caller-owned txn via a `SAVEPOINT`, instead of the old rollback-then-re-read-on-a-fresh-connection.

## Design & mechanism

The concrete `Transaction` wraps a SeaORM `DatabaseTransaction`; each `Pg*` adapter recovers it by downcast (`as_any()`), keeping the per-aggregate ports separate and `dyn`-safe. The application layer stays free of any `Generations` import (it bumps via a `PolicyGenBumper` port). The UoW mechanism was de-risked first (its own commit/rollback/savepoint-isolation tests against real Postgres) before the six mutation sites were routed through it. Implemented via subagent-driven TDD with a per-task review gate and an Opus whole-branch review (verdict: **READY**). Spec + plan in `docs/superpowers/`.

## Testing

- **Unit (fakes):** per-site event/audit/correlation construction; the D2 guard (a rolled-back mutation emits nothing and never bumps/evicts); savepoint absorb-vs-conflict; relay drain/park.
- **Real Postgres (testcontainers):** UoW commit/rollback/savepoint mechanism; per-aggregate atomicity (aggregate + outbox + audit share a correlation id); the SMA-444 policy conflict semantics preserved through the savepoint; api-key issue with **no secret** in payload/detail; relay SKIP-LOCKED isolation + poison-park; and an **e2e** driving a real authorized role-grant over HTTP → correlated `role_grant` + `event_outbox` + `audit_log` rows → one relay tick publishes.
- **Full `moon ci` green** (the affected `iam-core` + `iam` build/test/lint/fmt + machete); 484 iam tests. Preserves all SMA-444/445 behavior (revoke idempotency, duplicate-email/name `Conflict`, D15 anti-escalation, system-immutable).

## Follow-ups (separate issues/PRs, all "Part of SMA-446")

- Gateway service + IAM integration; Prometheus dashboards + RUNBOOK.
- Audit-log partitioning/retention; outbox pruning + a full dead-letter subsystem; a real (broker) `EventPublisher`; authz fail-closed hardening.
- A system-actor audit row for bootstrap-admin grants (the cold-start seeder deliberately bypasses `RoleService::grant`, so it currently emits neither event nor audit).

content.text:
Makes sense — I'd rather brainstorm from the real design than guess. Please share the AI Gateway PRD. Two easy ways:

- **Paste** its key points here, or
- **Give me the Notion link** (or a title to search) — I have Notion access and can fetch it directly. The SMA-446 issue referenced Notion IAM pages, so the PRD is likely alongside them.

To scope #2 well, the decisions I most need from it:

1. **Where the gateway lives** — is the `paigasus-gateway` crate in *this* repo meant to become the AI Gateway, or does the real gateway live in a separate product/repo (making #2 here mostly the IAM-side contract)?
2. **Upstream & request model** — what does the gateway proxy to (LLM providers? which? one or many?), and what's the request shape (OpenAI-compatible? streaming?).
3. **"Virtual keys" today** — how does the current AI Gateway authenticate callers (the self-contained key store the epic says to remove), and what does the **cutover to IAM-issued keys** entail (hard switch vs. dual-run — the epic's open question)?
4. **Authz mapping** — what resource/action should the gateway pass to IAM `is_authorized` per request (e.g. project-scoped model access)? What's the principal (the API key's service account)?
5. **Scope for now** — the PRD's MVP vs. the full vision, so we can decompose #2 like we did M5.

Once you drop the PRD (or the link), I'll run the brainstorm → adversarial challenge → **GATE 1**, then plan and implement — same pipeline as Slice A/B. I'll pause here for that.

content: And yes the paigasus-gateway crate is meant to become the AI gateway

{"metadata":{"type":"page"},"title":"AI Gateway","url":"https://app.notion.com/p/385830e8fbaa809dbe29ff5deb10cc17","text":"Here is the result of "view" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/385830e8fbaa809dbe29ff5deb10cc17 as of 2026-06-20T11:51:30.320Z: {"title":"AI Gateway"} > **TL;DR** — Build **Paigasus AI Gateway**, a Rust service that sits in front of every LLM provider Paigasus uses and exposes a single, drop-in endpoint. It accepts **both** OpenAI-compatible **and** Anthropic-compatible REST requests, normalizes them to a canonical internal model, routes to the right provider with retries/fallback/load-balancing, and adds the operational layer LiteLLM is known for: virtual keys + auth + rate limiting, cost tracking + budgets, and caching + observability. It is the first project landing in `paigasus-core` and the control point through which all future Paigasus AI workflows make model calls. *Status: Scoping · Owner: Sven · Last updated: 2026-06-20* --- ## 1. Context & motivation Paigasus has two goals: become a platform for the entire AI lifecycle, and ship common, out-of-the-box AI-powered workflows. Every one of those workflows ultimately makes model calls — and today each would have to deal with provider SDKs, auth, retries, cost, and failover on its own. An AI gateway is the natural **foundation layer**: it centralizes provider access so the rest of the platform (and external consumers) talk to one stable, observable, governed interface. Doing it in Rust fits Paigasus's "Rust-first for mission-critical paths" stance: the gateway is on the hot path of every request, so latency overhead, memory footprint, and reliability matter, and a compiled async core (tokio + tower) buys us low, predictable overhead. It also makes a strong **first** project for `paigasus-core`: it exercises the full toolchain (Moon, hexagonal service crate, eventual `contracts/` + `paigasus-kernel` bindings) on something genuinely useful rather than a toy. LiteLLM is the reference point for *what* a gateway should do. Our intent is not to clone it but to build a Rust-native, open-core gateway with first-class Paigasus integration and **dual OpenAI + Anthropic ingress** as a differentiator. ## 2. Goals - A single endpoint that is **wire-compatible with both the OpenAI and the Anthropic REST APIs**, so existing SDKs/clients of either point at the gateway with only a base-URL change. - **Unified routing** across OpenAI, Anthropic, Google (Gemini/Vertex), Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, and local/self-hosted (Ollama/vLLM) with retries, fallback, and load-balancing across deployments of the same logical model. - **Governance**: virtual keys scoped per team/user/project, with per-key model allowlists and RPM/TPM rate limits. - **Cost control**: per-request token→cost accounting aggregated per key/team/model, with soft and hard budgets. - **Operability**: response caching, structured request logs, metrics, and distributed tracing for every call. - **Extensibility**: adding a new provider is implementing one trait, not touching the core. - Land cleanly in `paigasus-core` under its conventions (Moon, hexagonal service, edition 2024 / rust 1.95, SPDX headers, ADRs). ## 3. Non-goals (for v1) - A web admin UI / dashboard (config is file + API driven in v1; UI is later). - gRPC and `contracts/`-generated APIs (REST-only ingress for v1; see Open Questions). - Agent orchestration, tool-calling routing logic, RAG, or prompt management — the gateway proxies calls, it does not own application logic. - Fine-tuning, batch, files, assistants, and other non-inference provider endpoints (chat/completions, messages, embeddings only in v1). - Semantic caching (v1 ships exact-match caching; semantic is roadmap). - Multi-region / HA topology design (single-deployment first; scale-out is a later concern). - Built-in guardrail *implementations* (PII redaction, content filtering, safety checks) — v1 ships only the **hook points** (a no-op `Guardrail` trait wired into the pipeline); concrete guardrails are a fast-follow that won't touch the core. See §6.6. ## 4. Prior art & competitive landscape
Project Lang What we take from it
**LiteLLM** Python The canonical feature set: virtual keys, cost tracking, budgets, fallbacks, 100+ providers, OpenAI-normalized I/O. Our functional reference.
**TensorZero** Rust Industrial Rust gateway; evidence the Rust approach scales. Watch their canonical-schema design.
**Helicone AI Gateway** Rust Low-latency (\~50ms) unify + telemetry; bar for observability ergonomics.
**Traceloop Hub** Rust OpenTelemetry-native gateway; reference for OTel integration.
**api7 AISIX** Rust Unified OpenAI-compatible API + hot-reload config via etcd + OTel; reference for config/reload.
**Where Paigasus differentiates:** (1) **dual ingress** — native OpenAI *and* Anthropic wire formats in and out, not just OpenAI-normalized; (2) deep Paigasus platform integration (kernel, shared contracts, IAM) so the gateway is the backbone of the wider lifecycle platform, not a standalone proxy; (3) Apache-2.0 open-core. ## 5. Personas - **App developer** — points an existing OpenAI or Anthropic SDK at the gateway; wants drop-in compatibility, streaming, and reliability without code changes. - **Platform / SRE operator** — configures providers/deployments, issues virtual keys, sets budgets and limits, watches metrics and traces. - **Paigasus internal workflows** — out-of-the-box workflows call the gateway as their single model backend. - **Finance / team lead** — reads spend per team/project against budgets. ## 6. Functional requirements ### 6.1 Ingress (dual wire-compatible REST) - **OpenAI-compatible**: `POST /v1/chat/completions`, `POST /v1/embeddings`, `GET /v1/models` (+ legacy `/v1/completions`). SSE streaming for chat. - **Anthropic-compatible**: `POST /v1/messages`, `GET /v1/models` (Anthropic shape). SSE streaming with Anthropic event types. - Both ingress formats deserialize into one **canonical internal request model**; the client's wire format determines the response wire format (OpenAI-in → OpenAI-out, Anthropic-in → Anthropic-out), including streaming event translation. ### 6.2 Routing, reliability & providers - Map a requested model name to one or more **deployments** (provider + credentials + upstream model). - **Retries** with backoff on transient errors; **fallback** to alternate deployments/models; **load-balancing** (round-robin / weighted / least-busy) across deployments of one logical model. - Per-deployment **cooldown** on repeated failures / rate-limit responses. - Provider egress adapters (v1 target set): **OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Google Vertex AI, Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, local OpenAI-compatible (Ollama/vLLM)**. Each implements a single `ProviderAdapter` trait (canonical→wire, wire→canonical, streaming). ### 6.3 Virtual keys, auth & rate limiting - Issue/revoke **virtual API keys** bound to a team/user/project; master admin key for management. - Per-key **model allowlist** and metadata; keys validated on every request. - **RPM/TPM rate limits** per key (and optionally per team/model), enforced via a shared counter store; standard `429` + rate-limit headers. ### 6.4 Cost tracking & budgets - Compute **token usage → cost** per request from a configurable price table per model/provider. - Persist **spend logs**; aggregate per key/team/model/time window. - **Soft budgets** (warn / log / alert) and **hard budgets** (reject with `402/429`) per key and team. ### 6.5 Caching & observability - **Exact-match response cache** (keyed on normalized request) with TTL and per-key opt-out; cache hit/miss surfaced in logs and a response header. - **Structured JSON logs** per request (model, deployment, latency, tokens, cost, cache status, key/team — never prompt/PII by default). - **Metrics** (Prometheus) and **distributed tracing** (OpenTelemetry) covering ingress → routing → egress. ### 6.6 Guardrail hook points (stub only) - Define a `Guardrail` trait with **request** (on canonical request, pre-routing), **response** (on canonical response), and **streaming-chunk** interception points, each able to pass / mutate / reject. - Wire the hooks into the pipeline as an ordered, configurable chain; v1 ships a **no-op pass-through** implementation only. - Goal: concrete guardrails (PII redaction, content filtering, safety checks) are added later as new `Guardrail` impls with **zero core changes** — the same extensibility contract as `ProviderAdapter`. ## 7. Non-functional requirements - **Latency overhead**: added gateway overhead p99 \< 15 ms for non-streaming (excluding upstream provider time); streaming first-token passthrough with no added buffering. - **Throughput**: handle thousands of concurrent in-flight streamed connections on a single node (async, no per-request thread). - **Reliability**: a single failing provider/deployment must not take down the gateway; graceful degradation via fallback + cooldown. - **Security**: provider credentials and virtual keys stored hashed/encrypted at rest; secrets never logged; TLS terminated in front; constant-time key comparison. - **Extensibility**: new provider = new `ProviderAdapter` impl, zero core changes; new ingress dialect is additive. - **Configurability**: declarative config (providers, deployments, model groups, price table) loadable from file + env; **hot-reload** as a fast-follow. - **Observability-by-default**: every request traceable end-to-end. ## 8. Architecture sketch Hexagonal service crate, per `paigasus-core` conventions. Pure routing/normalization logic lives in a `libs` crate so it stays testable and bindable; the service crate wires adapters. ```javascript rs/crates/ libs/ paigasus-gateway-core/ # pure domain: canonical model, routing policy, # budget/limit rules, request/response normalization, # Guardrail trait + chain services/ paigasus-ai-gateway/ # binary (hexagonal) domain/ # entities: VirtualKey, Team, Deployment, ModelGroup, Budget, SpendLog application/ # use cases: HandleChat, HandleMessages, Route, EnforceLimits, RecordSpend adapters/ ingress/ # OpenAI + Anthropic HTTP (axum) → canonical egress/ # ProviderAdapter impls (OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini/Vertex/Azure/Bedrock/local) persistence/ # SeaORM + Postgres (keys, budgets, spend logs, config) cache/ # Redis (cache + rate-limit counters) guardrails/ # Guardrail trait impls (v1: no-op pass-through) telemetry/ # tracing + OTel + Prometheus config/ ``` **Request flow:** ingress adapter deserializes (OpenAI or Anthropic) → canonical request → auth + rate-limit + budget checks → **request guardrail chain (no-op in v1)** → cache lookup → router picks deployment → egress adapter calls provider (with retry/fallback) → provider response → canonical → **response/stream guardrail chain (no-op in v1)** → re-serialized to the client's wire format → spend recorded, metrics/trace emitted. **Tech choices (consistent with existing Paigasus stack):** `axum` + `tower` (shares the tower/tonic ecosystem; middleware for auth/limits/tracing), `reqwest` for egress, `tokio`, `SeaORM` + PostgreSQL (as in the IAM service), `Redis` for counters + cache, `tracing`/`tracing-subscriber` + `opentelemetry`. Internal canonical request/response is the single source of truth; ingress and egress are pure (de)serialization at the edges. ## 9. Core data model (v1)
Entity Purpose
`VirtualKey` Hashed key, owner (team/user/project), model allowlist, rate-limit + budget refs, status.
`Team` / `Project` Grouping for budgets, limits, and spend aggregation.
`Provider` Provider type + credentials (encrypted) + base config.
`Deployment` A concrete (provider, upstream model, credentials) target.
`ModelGroup` Logical model name → set of `Deployment`s + routing/fallback policy.
`PriceEntry` Per-model input/output token prices for cost calc.
`SpendLog` Per-request: key, team, model, deployment, tokens, cost, latency, cache status, timestamp.
`Budget` Soft/hard limits + window, attached to key or team.
## 10. Milestones (phased delivery) Each milestone is an end-to-end vertical slice and maps to a Linear epic (`SMA-NNN`).
# Milestone Outcome
**M0** Walking skeleton axum service in `rs/crates/services/`, OpenAI `/v1/chat/completions` passthrough to **one** provider (OpenAI), SSE streaming, health check, structured logs. CI green in Moon.
**M1** Multi-provider routing + reliability `ProviderAdapter` trait; add Anthropic, Gemini/Vertex, Azure, Bedrock, local; model groups, retries, fallback, load-balancing, cooldown.
**M2** Dual Anthropic ingress `/v1/messages` ingress + Anthropic-shaped responses & streaming; canonical model proven across both dialects.
**M3** Virtual keys, auth & rate limiting Key issue/revoke, allowlists, RPM/TPM via Redis, master admin key, persistence in Postgres.
**M4** Cost tracking & budgets Price table, token→cost, spend logs, per-key/team aggregation, soft + hard budgets.
**M5** Caching & observability Exact-match cache, Prometheus metrics, OTel traces end-to-end, cache headers, dashboards/runbook.
(Sequencing note: v1 was scoped to include **all** capability pillars. M0–M2 deliver the irreducible proxy; M3–M5 add the operational layer. Pillars can be re-ordered, but routing must land first. The no-op guardrail hook points land with the pipeline scaffolding in M0–M1 so later milestones and fast-follows can slot real guardrails in without refactoring.) ## 11. Decisions that need an ADR Per Paigasus convention, significant choices get a Notion ADR before code: - **Canonical internal model design** — the schema both OpenAI and Anthropic dialects map to (incl. tool calls, multimodal, streaming events). The riskiest design decision. - **Dual ingress/egress strategy** — how round-tripping preserves provider-specific fields without lossy normalization. - **Datastore choice** — SeaORM + Postgres for durable state; Redis for counters/cache. Confirm vs. alternatives. - **Rate-limit algorithm** — token bucket vs. sliding window; Redis-backed vs. in-process for single-node. - **Provider credential & virtual-key secret handling** — encryption at rest, rotation, KMS vs. env. - **Config format & hot-reload** — file schema, reload mechanism (watch vs. signal vs. control API). - **Streaming normalization** — translating SSE event shapes between OpenAI and Anthropic without added latency. - **Guardrail interface** — the `Guardrail` trait shape, chain ordering, and how a guardrail may mutate vs. reject across request / response / streaming-chunk points (sync vs. async). ## 12. Risks & open questions - **Canonical-model leakage** — over-normalizing loses provider-specific features (e.g., Anthropic thinking blocks, OpenAI tool schemas). Mitigation: passthrough escape hatch + provider-extension fields. - **Scope size** — all four pillars in "v1" is large for a first project; phasing (M0–M5) keeps each slice shippable, but expect v1 to be several months of part-time work. - **Provider drift** — APIs change often; isolate per-adapter and version-pin behaviors. - **Cost accuracy** — token counts/prices vary by provider and may need reconciliation against provider-reported usage. - **Open: gRPC / ****`contracts/`** — deferred for v1, but should the canonical model be defined in `contracts/` (buf) from the start so a future gRPC surface and `paigasus-kernel` bindings come for free? - **Open: relationship to existing IAM service** — reuse `paigasus-iam-service` concepts/auth, or keep gateway keys self-contained in v1? - **Guardrails (resolved 2026-06-20)** — v1 stubs **minimal hook points** (no-op `Guardrail` trait + chain, §6.6); concrete guardrail implementations are a fast-follow. ## 13. Success metrics - A real OpenAI **and** a real Anthropic SDK work unmodified against the gateway (base-URL swap only), including streaming. - Gateway overhead within the p99 \< 15 ms target under load. - ≥ 1 fallback scenario demonstrably recovers a failed primary deployment with no client-visible error. - Spend per team/model is queryable and matches provider-reported usage within tolerance. - A new provider adapter can be added in a single PR touching only its adapter module. --- *Next steps: confirm the open questions (esp. **`contracts/`** timing and IAM reuse), then break M0–M5 into Linear epics/issues and open the canonical-model ADR.* "}

Pure routing/normalization logic lives in a `libs` crate so it stays testable and bindable; the service crate wires adapters. ```javascript rs/crates/ libs/ paigasus-gateway-core/ # pure domain: canonical model, routing policy, # budget/limit rules, request/response normalization, # Guardrail trait + chain services/ paigasus-ai-gateway/ # binary (hexagonal) domain/ # entities: VirtualKey, Team, Deployment, ModelGroup, Budget, SpendLog application/ # use cases: HandleChat, HandleMessages, Route, EnforceLimits, RecordSpend adapters/ ingress/ # OpenAI + Anthropic HTTP (axum) → canonical egress/ # ProviderAdapter impls (OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini/Vertex/Azure/Bedrock/local) persistence/ # SeaORM + Postgres (keys, budgets, spend logs, config) cache/ # Redis (cache + rate-limit counters) guardrails/ # Guardrail trait impls (v1: no-op pass-through) telemetry/ # tracing + OTel + Prometheus config/ ``` **Request flow:** ingress adapter deserializes (OpenAI or Anthropic) → canonical request → auth + rate-limit + budget checks → **request guardrail chain (no-op in v1)** → cache lookup → router picks deployment → egress adapter calls provider (with retry/fallback) → provider response → canonical → **response/stream guardrail chain (no-op in v1)** → re-serialized to the client's wire format → spend recorded, metrics/trace emitted. **Tech choices (consistent with existing Paigasus stack):** `axum` + `tower` (shares the tower/tonic ecosystem; middleware for auth/limits/tracing), `reqwest` for egress, `tokio`, `SeaORM` + PostgreSQL (as in the IAM service), `Redis` for counters + cache, `tracing`/`tracing-subscriber` + `opentelemetry`. Internal canonical request/response is the single source of truth; ingress and egress are pure (de)serialization at the edges. ## 9. Core data model (v1)
Entity Purpose
`VirtualKey` Hashed key, owner (team/user/project), model allowlist, rate-limit + budget refs, status.
`Team` / `Project` Grouping for budgets, limits, and spend aggregation.
`Provider` Provider type + credentials (encrypted) + base config.
`Deployment` A concrete (provider, upstream model, credentials) target.
`ModelGroup` Logical model name → set of `Deployment`s + routing/fallback policy.
`PriceEntry` Per-model input/output token prices for cost calc.
`SpendLog` Per-request: key, team, model, deployment, tokens, cost, latency, cache status, timestamp.
`Budget` Soft/hard limits + window, attached to key or team.
## 10. Milestones (phased delivery) Each milestone is an end-to-end vertical slice and maps to a Linear epic (`SMA-NNN`).
# Milestone Outcome
**M0** Walking skeleton axum service in `rs/crates/services/`, OpenAI `/v1/chat/completions` passthrough to **one** provider (OpenAI), SSE streaming, health check, structured logs. CI green in Moon.
**M1** Multi-provider routing + reliability `ProviderAdapter` trait; add Anthropic, Gemini/Vertex, Azure, Bedrock, local; model groups, retries, fallback, load-balancing, cooldown.
**M2** Dual Anthropic ingress `/v1/messages` ingress + Anthropic-shaped responses & streaming; canonical model proven across both dialects.
**M3** Virtual keys, auth & rate limiting Key issue/revoke, allowlists, RPM/TPM via Redis, master admin key, persistence in Postgres.
**M4** Cost tracking & budgets Price table, token→cost, spend logs, per-key/team aggregation, soft + hard budgets.
**M5** Caching & observability Exact-match cache, Prometheus metrics, OTel traces end-to-end, cache headers, dashboards/runbook.
(Sequencing note: v1 was scoped to include **all** capability pillars. M0–M2 deliver the irreducible proxy; M3–M5 add the operational layer. Pillars can be re-ordered, but routing must land first. The no-op guardrail hook points land with the pipeline scaffolding in M0–M1 so later milestones and fast-follows can slot real guardrails in without refactoring.) ## 11. Decisions that need an ADR Per Paigasus convention, significant choices get a Notion ADR before code: - **Canonical internal model design** — the schema both OpenAI and Anthropic dialects map to (incl. tool calls, multimodal, streaming events). The riskiest design decision. - **Dual ingress/egress strategy** — how round-tripping preserves provider-specific fields without lossy normalization. - **Datastore choice** — SeaORM + Postgres for durable state; Redis for counters/cache. Confirm vs. alternatives. - **Rate-limit algorithm** — token bucket vs. sliding window; Redis-backed vs. in-process for single-node. - **Provider credential & virtual-key secret handling** — encryption at rest, rotation, KMS vs. env. - **Config format & hot-reload** — file schema, reload mechanism (watch vs. signal vs. control API). - **Streaming normalization** — translating SSE event shapes between OpenAI and Anthropic without added latency. - **Guardrail interface** — the `Guardrail` trait shape, chain ordering, and how a guardrail may mutate vs. reject across request / response / streaming-chunk points (sync vs. async). ## 12. Risks & open questions - **Canonical-model leakage** — over-normalizing loses provider-specific features (e.g., Anthropic thinking blocks, OpenAI tool schemas). Mitigation: passthrough escape hatch + provider-extension fields. - **Scope size** — all four pillars in "v1" is large for a first project; phasing (M0–M5) keeps each slice shippable, but expect v1 to be several months of part-time work. - **Provider drift** — APIs change often; isolate per-adapter and version-pin behaviors. - **Cost accuracy** — token counts/prices vary by provider and may need reconciliation against provider-reported usage. - **Open: gRPC / ****`contracts/`** — deferred for v1, but should the canonical model be defined in `contracts/` (buf) from the start so a future gRPC surface and `paigasus-kernel` bindings come for free? - **Open: relationship to existing IAM service** — reuse `paigasus-iam-service` concepts/auth, or keep gateway keys self-contained in v1? - **Guardrails (resolved 2026-06-20)** — v1 stubs **minimal hook points** (no-op `Guardrail` trait + chain, §6.6); concrete guardrail implementations are a fast-follow. ## 13. Success metrics - A real OpenAI **and** a real Anthropic SDK work unmodified against the gateway (base-URL swap only), including streaming. - Gateway overhead within the p99 \< 15 ms target under load. - ≥ 1 fallback scenario demonstrably recovers a failed primary deployment with no client-visible error. - Spend per team/model is queryable and matches provider-reported usage within tolerance. - A new provider adapter can be added in a single PR touching only its adapter module. --- *Next steps: confirm the open questions (esp. **`contracts/`** timing and IAM reuse), then break M0–M5 into Linear epics/issues and open the canonical-model ADR.* "}

content.text:
Got it — the PRD is comprehensive, and you've confirmed the `paigasus-gateway` crate becomes the AI Gateway. Here's my read and the scoping decision.

## What the PRD says (and how it meets SMA-446)

The **AI Gateway** is a full Rust product — dual OpenAI+Anthropic ingress, a canonical model, multi-provider routing/fallback, virtual keys+auth+rate-limiting, cost/budgets, caching+observability, guardrail hooks — with its **own** phased milestones **M0–M5** (walking skeleton → multi-provider → dual ingress → keys/auth/rate-limit → cost → caching/obs). The PRD estimates *"several months of part-time work"* for v1.

The key intersection: the PRD's **§12 open question** — *"reuse IAM, or keep gateway keys self-contained in v1?"* — is exactly what **SMA-446 says it resolves**: the gateway consumes IAM (IAM-issued keys + `is_authorized`), **not** a self-contained key store. IAM is now fully built to support that (`IntrospectApiKey`, `IsAuthorized`).

## The scoping reality

You **can't integrate IAM into a gateway that doesn't exist yet** — it's still a `fn main(){}` stub. So sub-project #2 is really the **start of the gateway product**, and the natural, buildable first slice is the PRD's **M0 walking skeleton — but with IAM as the auth/authz backbone from day one** (resolving the IAM-reuse open question in code, per SMA-446). The gateway's M1–M5 (multi-provider, dual ingress, rate-limit/cost/caching) become their own follow-up epics.

That gives a coherent vertical slice: *an axum gateway that authenticates a caller's IAM-issued key via `IntrospectApiKey`, authorizes the request via `IsAuthorized`, and proxies `POST /v1/chat/completions` (SSE streaming) to OpenAI* — the "prove the gateway consumes IAM" outcome SMA-446 wants, and the foundation the rest of the gateway builds on.

Before I spec it, two decisions the PRD explicitly leaves open shape the whole thing:

content.text:
Both locked in: **#2 = gateway M0 walking skeleton + IAM auth** (OpenAI `/v1/chat/completions` passthrough with SSE → OpenAI, authn via `IntrospectApiKey`, authz via `IsAuthorized`), **REST-only Rust structs** (canonical model + `contracts/` deferred to M1/M2).

One design fork remains that needs your call — the **authz mapping**. The gateway must call `IsAuthorized(principal, action, resource)` per request, but IAM's action catalog is all tenancy/authz/SA/key-management — there's **no "invoke model / use gateway" action** yet. Let me confirm what `IntrospectApiKey` hands back, then put the fork to you.

content.text: `IntrospectApiKey` returns the SA `principal_prn` + `status` + `memberships` + `role_grants`; the `ApiKey` itself has a `scope_prn` (its team/project) and `scope_actions` ("stored, unenforced in v1"). `IsAuthorized` takes `(principal_prn, action, resource_prn, context)`. So the gateway has the SA identity and its tenancy, but **there's no model-invocation action in IAM's Cedar catalog** — that's the fork:

A real is_authorized gate (meets the AC) with minimal plumbing — no need to surface the key's project. Project/team-scoped authz + per-key model allowlists come in a later gateway milestone. My recommendation for M0.

# SMA-446 (#2) — AI Gateway M0 walking skeleton + IAM-backed auth

**Status:** Design (brainstormed) · **Date:** 2026-07-13 · **Linear:** SMA-446 (Part of; the
"gateway consumes IAM" AC) · **Crates:** `paigasus-gateway` (service) + IAM changes in
`paigasus-iam` / `paigasus-iam-core` / `contracts` / `paigasus-proto`.

---

## 1. Context

The [AI Gateway PRD](https://app.notion.com/p/385830e8fbaa809dbe29ff5deb10cc17) describes a full
Rust LLM gateway (dual OpenAI+Anthropic ingress, canonical model, multi-provider routing, virtual
keys/auth/rate-limit, cost/budgets, caching/observability) delivered across its own milestones
**M0–M5**. Its §12 open question — *"reuse IAM, or keep gateway keys self-contained?"* — is the one
**SMA-446 resolves: the gateway consumes IAM** (IAM-issued keys + `is_authorized`), no
self-contained key store.

The `paigasus-gateway` crate is currently a `fn main(){}` stub. You cannot integrate IAM into a
gateway that doesn't exist, so this sub-project is the **start of the gateway product**: the PRD's
**M0 walking skeleton, with IAM as the auth/authz backbone from day one**. IAM (merged M1–M5) now
exposes exactly what's needed: `AuthnService.IntrospectApiKey`, `AuthorizationService.IsAuthorized`.

**Scope decided with Sven:** M0 + IAM auth; REST-only Rust structs (canonical model + `contracts/`
deferred to gateway M1/M2); authz = a **new project-scoped `InvokeModel` Cedar action**.

## 2. Goals / Non-goals

### Goals (this slice)
- **G1.** A real `paigasus-gateway` axum service exposing `POST /v1/chat/completions`
  (OpenAI-wire-compatible, **SSE streaming + non-streaming**) that proxies to the **OpenAI**
  upstream (`reqwest`), plus a health endpoint and structured JSON request logs.
- **G2.** Every request is **authenticated via IAM**: the caller's bearer token is an IAM-issued
  API key; the gateway calls `IntrospectApiKey` → rejects invalid/inactive/expired (`401`), else
  resolves the service-account principal + the key's scope.
- **G3.** Every request is **authorized via IAM**: `IsAuthorized(SA_prn, "InvokeModel",
  key.scope_prn)` → deny ⇒ `403` (IAM records the denial in its audit log, Slice A). The gateway
  holds the **real OpenAI credential** and swaps it in for the upstream call; the caller never
  sees it.
- **G4 (IAM-side):** add a **project-scoped `InvokeModel`** Cedar action to IAM, and surface the
  key's **`scope_prn`** on `IntrospectApiKeyResponse` so the gateway can authorize against the
  tenant.

### Non-goals (deferred to gateway M1–M5 / follow-ups)
- Multi-provider routing/fallback/load-balancing; Anthropic ingress; the canonical model +
  `contracts/`/gRPC surface; rate limiting; cost tracking/budgets; caching; guardrail impls
  (M0 may scaffold the no-op hook only if cheap, else defer); admin UI; other provider endpoints
  (`/v1/embeddings`, `/v1/models`, legacy `/v1/completions`) — **M0 is `/v1/chat/completions`
  only**.
- Enforcing the key's `scope_actions` model-allowlist (stored-but-unenforced in IAM v1) — later
  milestone.

## 3. Architecture

Hexagonal, in the existing `paigasus-gateway` service crate (a `paigasus-gateway-core` lib is
extracted when M1's routing/canonical-model needs pure testable logic — YAGNI for M0):

```
rs/crates/services/paigasus-gateway/
  src/
    main.rs                      # compose: config, IAM clients, upstream client, axum server, shutdown
    config.rs                    # [gateway] config + validate (+ gateway.toml.example)
    domain/                      # CallerContext { principal_prn, scope_prn, key_id }
    application/
      proxy_chat.rs              # the ChatCompletions use-case (authz already done by middleware)
    adapters/
      http/
        mod.rs                   # axum router: /healthz, /v1/chat/completions; auth middleware layer
        auth.rs                  # tower middleware: bearer → IAM authn+authz → CallerContext extension
        chat.rs                  # POST /v1/chat/completions handler (stream + non-stream)
        error.rs                 # OpenAI-shaped error envelope + status mapping
        dto.rs                   # OpenAI request/response structs (serde) — enough for model/stream/logging
      iam/
        client.rs                # tonic clients: AuthnServiceClient + AuthorizationServiceClient
      openai/
        client.rs                # reqwest client to the OpenAI upstream (non-stream + stream passthrough)
```

**Request flow:** `POST /v1/chat/completions` → **auth middleware** (bearer → `IntrospectApiKey`
→ active? → `IsAuthorized(SA, InvokeModel, scope_prn)`) → chat handler parses the OpenAI request
(for `model`/`stream` + logging) → **OpenAI egress** (`reqwest`, real OpenAI key) → non-stream:
return JSON; stream: pipe the upstream SSE body to the axum response with no buffering → structured
log (model, latency, status, caller — never prompt/PII).

**Tech:** `axum` + `tower` (matches IAM's stack), `reqwest` (egress, streaming), `tonic`
(IAM gRPC clients via `paigasus-proto`), `tokio`, `paigasus-logging`/`tracing`. New deps:
`reqwest` (with `stream`/`rustls-tls`), `tonic`/`prost` (already in the tree via `paigasus-proto`),
`axum`/`tower`/`tower-http`, `serde`/`serde_json`, `futures`/`tokio-stream`, `secrecy` for the
provider key. New workspace deps → `deny.toml`/`machete` review.

## 4. IAM-backed auth/authz (the SMA-446 core)

### 4.1 Transport — gRPC client to IAM
The gateway is a **tonic client** of IAM's `AuthnService`/`AuthorizationService` (generated in
`paigasus-proto`). Config: `iam.grpc_addr`. Per request = 2 IAM calls (`IntrospectApiKey` +
`IsAuthorized`); both are Redis-cached inside IAM (api-key validation cache + decision cache), so
the steady-state cost is a cache hit. (A combined introspect-and-authorize RPC is a possible future
optimization; out of scope for M0.)

### 4.2 Authn
`Authorization: Bearer <iam-key>` → `IntrospectApiKey{token}` →
- transport/`Unauthenticated`/not-found/inactive/expired ⇒ `401` (OpenAI-shaped error envelope);
- else read `principal_prn`, `status`, `key_id`, `expires_at`, **`scope_prn`** (new, §4.4). Reject
  if `status != active`. Build `CallerContext`.

### 4.3 Authz
`IsAuthorized{ principal_prn: SA, action: "InvokeModel", resource_prn: scope_prn }` →
- `allowed == false` ⇒ `403` (IAM already audited the denial with its determining policy);
- transport error ⇒ **fail-closed `403`** (a gateway that can't reach IAM must not grant access —
  distinct from IAM's own internal fail-open decision-cache posture, which is IAM's concern);
- `allowed == true` ⇒ proceed. `CallerContext` is attached as a request extension for the handler
  + logs.

### 4.4 IAM changes (bundled in this slice)
1. **`Action::InvokeModel`** — add to `paigasus-iam-core` `authz/action.rs` (enum + `ALL` +
   `as_wire()=="InvokeModel"` + `is_write` classification + the exhaustiveness test/`len`), and to
   the embedded Cedar `SCHEMA_SRC` (`authz/schema.rs`) in the shared action block (resource applies
   to `Organization/Team/Project` — the tenant scopes a key can have). **Archived-project safety:**
   classify `InvokeModel` so an **archived** project denies it — either mark it `is_write`
   (the `forbid-archived-writes` policy then blocks it on archived nodes) or add a dedicated
   forbid rule. *(Decision to confirm in the plan: `is_write=true` is the simplest reuse; a model
   call arguably isn't a tenancy "write", so a dedicated `forbid InvokeModel on archived` rule may
   read cleaner — see §9 D5.)*
2. **Grant it in the starter roles** — add `InvokeModel` to the `org_member`/`team_member`/
   `project_member` (and the corresponding admin) action allowlists in `authz/roles.rs`, so a
   service account holding any membership role at/above its key's scope may invoke. (A dedicated
   `gateway_user` role is a possible later refinement.)
3. **`scope_prn` on `IntrospectApiKeyResponse`** — add `string scope_prn = 7;` to `iam.proto`,
   `buf format -w` + regenerate rs/py/ts bindings, and populate it in IAM's `IntrospectApiKey`
   handler from the key's stored `scope_prn` (the `ApiKey.scope_prn` already persisted in M4).

## 5. OpenAI passthrough + streaming

- The chat handler deserializes the body into an OpenAI-shaped `ChatCompletionRequest` (fields
  needed: `model`, `stream`, `messages`, plus `#[serde(flatten)] extra` to preserve unknown
  provider fields losslessly — the passthrough escape hatch), for `model`/`stream`/logging, then
  re-serializes to the upstream. (M0 could forward raw bytes, but a typed parse buys `model`/
  `stream` + validation cheaply.)
- **Non-streaming** (`stream != true`): `reqwest` POST to `<upstream.base_url>/v1/chat/completions`
  with `Authorization: Bearer <real-openai-key>`; return the upstream status + JSON body verbatim.
- **Streaming** (`stream == true`): request the upstream as a byte stream; return an axum
  `Body::from_stream` piping the upstream SSE chunks **unbuffered** (first-token passthrough, PRD
  NFR). Map upstream/transport errors to an OpenAI-shaped error (and, mid-stream, a terminal SSE
  error event where practical).
- Upstream errors (4xx/5xx from OpenAI) are surfaced with their status; a gateway-side failure
  (timeout, connect) → `502`/`504` OpenAI-shaped.

## 6. Config & secrets

`[gateway]` (in a new `config.rs` + `gateway.toml.example`), validated at boot:
- `http_addr`, `request_timeout_secs`.
- `iam.grpc_addr` (+ TLS later).
- `upstream.openai.base_url` (default `https://api.openai.com`), `upstream.openai.api_key`
  (a **secret** — `secrecy::SecretString`, from env; never logged; constant-time not needed as it's
  outbound, but never serialized into logs/errors).
- `log_level`.

## 7. Testing

- **Unit:** config validation; the OpenAI DTO round-trips + `extra` passthrough; the error-envelope
  mapping (transport→401/403/502); the auth-middleware decision table over **fake IAM clients**
  (invalid key→401; inactive→401; authz deny→403; IAM transport error→fail-closed 403; allow→pass +
  `CallerContext` populated).
- **Integration (the gateway's own tests):** boot the router with a **mock IAM gRPC server**
  (an in-process tonic server returning canned Introspect/IsAuthorized) + a **mock OpenAI upstream**
  (an in-process axum server) → drive `POST /v1/chat/completions` (a) unauthorized bearer → 401,
  (b) authz-denied SA → 403, (c) allowed → 200 with the mock upstream's body, (d) `stream:true` →
  the SSE chunks arrive in order, unbuffered. (Follows the IAM `tests/support` mock-server idiom.)
- **IAM-side:** `InvokeModel` in the action catalog + schema-validates + a starter-policy table case
  (a `project_member` SA is allowed `InvokeModel` on its project; denied on another; denied on an
  archived project); `IntrospectApiKey` returns the persisted `scope_prn` (a real-PG test).
- A true end-to-end against the real OpenAI API is **manual/out-of-band** (needs a live key); CI
  uses the mock upstream.

## 8. CI / gate considerations

- **New workspace deps** (`reqwest`, `secrecy`, `tokio-stream`, `futures`, `axum`/`tower-http` if
  not already present) → likely `rs/deny.toml` `[licenses] exceptions` / a dev advisory ignore, and
  a temporary `machete` `ignored` for any dep consumed a commit later than introduced. Run the full
  gate list.
- **Proto change** (`scope_prn`) → `buf format -w` + regen rs/py/ts bindings; additive → `:breaking`
  clean (verify). The embedded `FILE_DESCRIPTOR_SET` shifts → regen.
- **Affected-graph:** `paigasus-gateway` already `dependsOn` `paigasus-proto` + `paigasus-kernel`;
  it does **not** dependOn `paigasus-iam` (it talks over gRPC), so the `kernel->bindings`
  strict-equality set is unaffected. Confirm `:affected-smoke`.
- `wasm-getrandom-free`: the gateway is a native service (not wasm-bound) — unaffected; keep any
  shared/kernel crates untouched.
- Windows-reserved-name check: no `CON`/`PRN`/`AUX`/etc. source basenames.

## 9. Decision log

| # | Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Sub-project #2 = gateway **M0 walking skeleton + IAM auth** (not the full gateway) | Can't integrate IAM into a nonexistent gateway; M0 is the buildable first slice + the SMA-446 "consumes IAM" proof |
| D2 | **REST-only Rust structs**; no canonical model / `contracts/` / gRPC ingress yet | PRD v1 non-goal; the canonical model is only needed at M1/M2 (multi-provider/dual-ingress) |
| D3 | Authn+authz via **IAM over gRPC** (`IntrospectApiKey` + `IsAuthorized`); no self-contained keys | Resolves the PRD IAM-reuse open question; IAM caches both calls |
| D4 | **`InvokeModel` Cedar action, project-scoped**; authorize against the key's `scope_prn` | Tenant-isolated model access; sets up per-project governance (Sven's choice) |
| D5 | Surface **`scope_prn` on `IntrospectApiKeyResponse`** (proto add) | The gateway needs the tenant resource to authorize against; the key already stores it |
| D6 | Gateway **fail-closed** when it can't reach IAM for authz | A gateway that can't authorize must not grant model access |
| D7 | M0 in the existing `paigasus-gateway` service crate; extract `paigasus-gateway-core` at M1 | YAGNI — M0's pure logic is thin |

## 10. Risks / open items for the plan

- **`InvokeModel` archived-project classification** (§4.4/D5) — `is_write=true` reuse vs. a
  dedicated forbid rule; pick one in the plan (a starter-policy test pins the behavior).
- **Which roles grant `InvokeModel`** — member+admin roles at org/team/project, or a dedicated
  `gateway_user` role. Plan picks the minimal set; a bootstrap SA must be able to invoke in the
  integration test.
- **Streaming error semantics** — mapping a mid-stream upstream failure to a client-visible SSE
  error without breaking the passthrough; the plan specifies the terminal-event behavior.
- **Secret handling** — the OpenAI key via `secrecy`; ensure it never reaches logs/error bodies
  (a test asserts it).
- **Proto/deny/machete churn** — the `scope_prn` regen + new gateway deps need the full gate run
  and likely deny/machete waivers.

## 11. Follow-ups (gateway M1–M5 + governance)

- M1 multi-provider routing/fallback + the `ProviderAdapter` trait + extract `paigasus-gateway-core`
  + the canonical-model ADR + `contracts/`.
- M2 Anthropic ingress; M3 rate limiting (per-key RPM/TPM) + enforcing the key `scope_actions`
  model-allowlist; M4 cost/budgets; M5 caching + gateway dashboards/RUNBOOK.
- IAM: a dedicated `gateway_user` role; a combined introspect-and-authorize RPC to halve per-request
  IAM round-trips.

content.text:
Analysis complete. I have grounded every finding in the actual code.

## Verdict: NEEDS REWORK
The central deliverable of SMA-446 — the gateway's IAM authorization call — is unbuildable as specified: `AuthorizationService.IsAuthorized` is bearer-enforced and its `decide_gated` self/admin exposure gate will reject the gateway's `IsAuthorized(SA, InvokeModel, scope_prn)` cross-principal query, and the spec never says what credential the gateway presents. Separately, the "just add `scope_prn` to the response and populate it in the handler" IAM change is materially under-scoped — the scope isn't carried by `Credential`, `PrincipalContext`, or the hot-path validation cache. The OpenAI-passthrough and CI/proto sections are solid, but these two gaps plus the absence of any spend guardrail on a real-credential proxy require rework before implementation.

## Findings

### BLOCKER
- **The `IsAuthorized` authz call cannot succeed as described** — The spec (§4.3, G3) has the gateway call `IsAuthorized(SA_prn, "InvokeModel", scope_prn)`. But `AuthorizationService` is *not* on IAM's `:path` exemption list (`authn.rs:111-113` exempts only health + `Introspect` + `IntrospectApiKey`), so the RPC requires the gateway to present its *own* bearer token; `AuthzGrpc::is_authorized` extracts the caller from that bearer (`authz.rs:84`) and runs `decide_gated` (`authorize.rs:75-80`), which — because `req.principal` (the caller's SA) `!= actor` (whatever identity the gateway authenticated as) — first requires `actor` to hold `Action::ListRoleGrants` at `scope_prn`. Result: unless the gateway authenticates as an org/platform admin at *every* tenant scope, IAM returns `PermissionDenied` before ever evaluating `InvokeModel`, and the gateway (mapping any non-OK Status to fail-closed 403) denies *every* request. The spec is silent on which bearer the gateway sends. | Why it matters: the feature's raison d'être (gateway consumes IAM authz) does not work; the naive implementation 403s everything, and the "fix" of giving the gateway platform-admin is a confused-deputy over-privilege. | Suggested fix: specify that the gateway forwards **the caller's own IAM key** as the `authorization` metadata on the `IsAuthorized` gRPC call and queries `principal_prn == the caller's own SA` — a self-query, which bypasses the `decide_gated` exposure gate (`authorize.rs:76`) and needs no gateway service credential. Add an integration-test case asserting the self-query path is taken.

### MAJOR
- **Surfacing `scope_prn` on introspect is far larger than "populate it in the handler"** — §4.4.3/D5 says the key "already stores it," but the introspect handler builds `IntrospectApiKeyResponse` purely from `PrincipalContext` (`convert.rs:308-327`), whose `principal.credential` is `Credential::ApiKey { key_id, expires_at }` — no scope. `AuthenticateApiKey::introspect` never carries the scope, and the cache-hit path (`resolve_cached`) has only `CachedValidation { principal_id, sa_status, expires_at, key_hash }` (`cache.rs:65-69`) — the `ApiKey.scope` (`api_key.rs:84`) is in hand only transiently in `resolve_uncached`. | Why it matters: to populate `scope_prn` you must thread scope through a core domain type (`Credential::ApiKey` or `PrincipalContext`) *and* the Redis-serialized `CachedValidation` on the hot path the whole api-key design is built around — or force a DB read on every introspect, defeating the cache the p99 story depends on. Getting the cache path wrong yields an empty/stale scope → wrong-tenant authz or blanket fail-closed 403. This also touches the parallel HTTP `IntrospectApiKeyResponseDto` (`dto.rs:502-509`) for parity. | Suggested fix: scope the plan to add `scope` to `CachedValidation` (with its serialization/eviction implications) and to `Credential::ApiKey` or `PrincipalContext`, update both the gRPC and HTTP DTOs, and add a cache-hit test asserting `scope_prn` is returned without a DB read.
- **Real-credential proxy with zero spend guardrails and no input limits** — M0 holds the real OpenAI key (§6) but has no rate limit, no cost budget (deferred to M3/M4), no request-body size cap, no per-model allowlist (`scope_actions` explicitly unenforced, §2 non-goals), and a single `request_timeout_secs` (§6) that would also kill long legitimate streams. Any authorized SA can drive unbounded spend on the most expensive model, and a large body has no stated ceiling. | Why it matters: security/cost hazard — the blast radius of one leaked/over-granted key is an unbounded OpenAI bill with no per-tenant attribution or throttle. | Suggested fix: state an explicit M0 deployment constraint (internal/non-prod, or a hard account-level cap) AND add concrete cheap guardrails now: a max request-body size (`tower_http::limit`/`DefaultBodyLimit`), separate connect/first-byte vs overall-stream timeouts, and optionally a `max_tokens` clamp. If none are acceptable, say why in the decision log.
- **Fail-closed maps IAM outages to `401`/`403`, which are non-retryable to OpenAI clients** — §4.2 maps an `IntrospectApiKey` transport error to `401`; §4.3 maps an `IsAuthorized` transport error to `403`. Both mean "IAM is unreachable," not "your credentials are bad." | Why it matters: OpenAI SDKs treat 401/403 as fatal (stop, rotate key) and only 429/5xx as retryable. An IAM blip makes every client give up permanently and churn keys, and the two codes are inconsistent for the same failure class. Combined with fail-closed-on-IAM, the gateway's availability is now hard-coupled to IAM's with no mitigation noted. | Suggested fix: map "cannot reach/evaluate IAM" to `503` (retryable), distinct from a genuine deny (`403`) or bad key (`401`); keep the deny-by-default posture but signal retryability. Explicitly document the IAM-availability coupling and its accepted mitigation (IAM HA / co-location).
- **Adding `InvokeModel` to member roles dilutes their documented read-only meaning** — §4.4.2 grants `InvokeModel` to `org_member`/`team_member`/`project_member`, whose consts are documented and tested as "reads only" (`roles.rs:89-90,122-123,150-151`). | Why it matters: the lowest-privilege membership tier gains a spend-capable action, silently changing the security meaning of "member" and staling the module invariants/docs; a read-only auditor SA could now invoke paid models. | Suggested fix: prefer the deferred dedicated `gateway_user` role *now* (it's cheap), or, if reusing member roles, update the `*_MEMBER_ACTIONS` docs and any "member = read-only" assertions and call the semantic change out explicitly in the decision log.
- **Archived-project classification for `InvokeModel` is left open but is load-bearing** — §4.4.1/§10 defer the `is_write=true` vs dedicated-forbid choice to "the plan." If the implementer picks `is_write=false` and omits a forbid, `forbid-archived-writes` (derived from `Action::ALL.filter(is_write && !is_restore)`, `roles.rs:251-255`) will *not* fire, so an archived project still authorizes model invocation. | Why it matters: an unresolved decision directly controls whether an archived tenant can spend money; "decide later" risks the fail-open hole. | Suggested fix: resolve it in the spec, not the plan — mandate the archived-deny outcome with the pinning test (§7 already lists "denied on an archived project"). Note that `is_write=true` semantically labels a model call a "tenancy write," so a dedicated `forbid InvokeModel on archived` reads cleaner; pick one explicitly.
- **Gateway↔IAM transport carries raw API keys; "TLS later" (§6) is unsafe** — With the recommended fix the gateway forwards the caller's raw key as gRPC bearer metadata *and* sends it in the `IntrospectApiKey` body — twice per request over `iam.grpc_addr`. | Why it matters: on any non-loopback deployment, plaintext gRPC leaks live IAM API keys in transit. | Suggested fix: require TLS/mTLS on `iam.grpc_addr` for M0 unless gateway and IAM are provably co-located/loopback; don't defer.

### MINOR
- **Mid-stream and client-disconnect semantics are underspecified** (§5, §10) — "a terminal SSE error event where practical" is not buildable as written (you can't change the HTTP status after 200 + first `data:` chunk), and cancellation propagation on client abort isn't addressed. Without explicit drop-propagation, a client disconnect can leave the upstream `reqwest` stream running (wasted tokens, leaked connection). Specify the exact mid-stream behavior (e.g. emit `data: {"error":...}` then close) and require that dropping the response cancels the upstream request; add a mid-stream-failure and a client-abort integration test (the current §7 (d) only covers the happy stream).
- **Egress/response header handling not specified** (§5) — the spec sets `Authorization: Bearer <real-key>` but never says it *strips* the caller's inbound `Authorization` (and other caller headers like `OpenAI-Organization`, cookies) before forwarding, nor which upstream response headers are passed back. Specify an explicit egress header allowlist and confirm the caller's bearer never reaches OpenAI.
- **OpenAI error-envelope shape is undefined** (§3 `error.rs`, §5) — "OpenAI-shaped error" needs the exact `{"error":{"message","type","param","code"}}` contract, or two engineers will produce different bodies that break SDK error handling.
- **Schema block vs "project-scoped" wording** (§4.4.1, D4) — the single shared `action ... appliesTo { resource: [Root, Organization, Team, Project] }` block (`schema.rs:19-26`) includes `Root`; D4 calls `InvokeModel` "project-scoped" while §4.4 grants it at org/team/project. Clarify whether `InvokeModel` joins the shared block (inherits `Root`, harmless since keys never scope to Root) or gets a resource-restricted declaration, and fix the "project-scoped" wording.
- **Exhaustiveness/`len` update sites** — adding `InvokeModel` requires arms in `as_wire` and `is_write` (`action.rs`, compiler-enforced) and bumping `Action::ALL.len() == 35` and its comment (`action.rs:270`). `Action::parse` is data-driven over `ALL` so needs no change. The spec mentions this; just enumerate the sites in the plan so none is missed.

### QUESTIONS
- Which bearer does the gateway present to `IsAuthorized` (see BLOCKER) — the caller's key (self-query) or a gateway service credential? This must be answered before implementation.
- `IntrospectApiKey` returns fully paged memberships (`authenticate_api_key.rs:251-271`) the gateway doesn't use. Is paying that per request acceptable for M0, or does this argue for bringing the deferred "combined introspect-and-authorize RPC" (§4.1, §11) into M0, since the exposure-gate wrinkle already complicates the two-call design?
- `/v1/models`: some OpenAI-compatible SDKs probe it on init. Have the target M0 client SDKs been confirmed not to require it, given it 404s?
- What is the gateway's readiness contract? `/healthz` (§3) is liveness; given fail-closed-on-IAM, should readiness verify IAM (and upstream) reachability so orchestration doesn't route to a gateway that will 401/403 everything?
- What happens if `IntrospectApiKey` returns an empty `scope_prn` (older key / plumbing bug)? IAM's `IsAuthorized` will fail PRN parse → fail-closed 403. Is silent deny acceptable, or should the gateway surface a distinct diagnostic?

## What's good
- **The CI/proto blast-radius analysis is genuinely thorough** (§8): additive `scope_prn = 7` on `IntrospectApiKeyResponse` (current max field is 6, `iam.proto:242-249`) is correctly non-breaking, and the spec anticipates `buf format -w`, py/ts regen, the `FILE_DESCRIPTOR_SET` shift, deny/machete waivers, the affected-graph `kernel->bindings` set (gateway rightly does not `dependsOn` IAM — `moon.yml:7-9`), and wasm/Windows-name gates. Preserve this checklist.
- **The allow-list-not-exclude-list authz posture is respected** — routing `InvokeModel` through explicit role allowlists and the exhaustive `is_write` classification (`action.rs:150-188`) matches the codebase's fail-closed convention (`roles.rs:19-25`); the design correctly adds to allowlists rather than deriving.
- **Fail-closed as the default authz posture** (D6) is the right call and aligns with IAM's own denial-audit path (`denial_audit.rs:188` records the probed principal, so `InvokeModel` denials are attributed to the caller SA out of the box) — the issue is only the *status code* and the missing self-query mechanics, not the posture.
- **Secret handling is called out concretely** (§6, §10): `secrecy::SecretString` for the OpenAI key with an explicit test that it never reaches logs/errors, and structured logs that exclude prompt/PII.

Relevant files: `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-core/rs/crates/services/paigasus-iam/src/adapters/grpc/authn.rs` (exemption list, lines 111-113), `.../grpc/authz.rs` (actor extraction, line 84), `.../application/authorize.rs` (`decide_gated`, lines 75-80), `.../grpc/convert.rs` (`to_introspect_api_key_response`, lines 308-327), `.../adapters/api_keys/cache.rs` (`CachedValidation`, lines 65-69), `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-core/rs/crates/libs/paigasus-iam-core/src/api_key.rs` (line 84), `.../authz/action.rs` (`is_write`/`ALL`/len, lines 150-188, 270), `.../authz/roles.rs` (member action lists + `forbid_archived_writes_source`, lines 89-90, 251-255), `.../adapters/authz/denial_audit.rs` (line 188), `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-core/contracts/proto/paigasus/iam/v1/iam.proto` (lines 242-249).
